transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (NovaDocs Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Platform Eng), Oliver Reed (CTO)

Summary (auto):
Redwood walkthrough focused on migration parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Discussed endpoint mappings, function calling, streaming, embeddings, rate limiting, dedicated vs hosted options, security/compliance checks, and a proposed 2-week pilot and benchmark.

Topics: parity mapping, API differences, performance/quantization, security (SOC2/KMS/SAML), pilot scope, next steps.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're excited to run through a migration walkthrough from openai, anthropic and together into redwood. um ravi and i will tag team - maya here is AE, ravi SE.
[00:16] Oliver: thanks maya, quick note - we're evaluating multiple providers but our main ask is parity, low friction swap, and predictable cost. we have some latency SLOs for our chat product.
[00:30] Maya: totally, that's what we'll focus on. ravi, do you want to show the mapping sheet first?
[00:36] Ravi: sure, um i'll share my screen - here's the parity spreadsheet, high level mapping: openai/chat.completions -> redwood/chat.generate; completions -> redwood/text.generate, function calling semantics map but the webhook behavior is slightly different, i'll show code samples in a sec.
[00:54] Samir: can you repeat the function calling bit - we rely heavily on tool calls and structured arguments, that was a pain point with some vendors.
[01:03] Ravi: yes so with openai style function calling, you send a functions JSON and the model returns a call. with redwood, we support the same pattern: you define schema, redwood will return a structured payload and we include the function name; we also stream partial events while preserving schema enforcement. note: the field names in the response are 'tool_call' and 'tool_args' in the current API, older transcriptions might say 'function' - small rename but easy map.
[01:32] Lena: okay, does that break any of our existing orchestration? we do some middleware that expects exact openai fields.
[01:39] Ravi: not if you add a tiny adapter - in the mapping sheet i included 3 example snippets: node, python, curl. for node it's a one-liner map for the response object. we'll share those afterwards.
[01:50] Oliver: what about streaming? we need token-level streaming to show partial assistant responses in UI.
[01:56] Maya: yes, redwood supports streaming with the same chunked semantics; small differences in event names - we emit 'delta' events and provide 'chunk_id' for reassembly, again we put snippets in the sheet. streaming latency is comparable to openai in hosted mode, and for dedicated/private you can get lower p50 with optimized runtimes.
[02:20] Samir: latency specifics? our SLO is p50 < 250ms for prompt of ~150 tokens and p95 < 800ms.
[02:28] Ravi: for hosted with rwd-3b-q8 we typically see p50 ~120-180ms for short contexts; for longer sequences and private/dedicated we can tune quantization and batching. i'll caveat that's workload dependent and suggest running a 1hr benchmark with your prompt set.
[02:45] Lena: good. what about embeddings - we have a vector db pipeline using text-embedding-ada-002 currently.
[02:52] Ravi: embeddings map to rwd-embed-v1; semantic similarity scores are within expected ranges. dimensions are 1536 - if you're using ada that should be fine. costs per embedding unit are in the pilot pricing doc. we'll provide conversion guidance; there are small differences in tokenization which can change costs slightly.
[03:12] Oliver: any pitfalls migrating from anthropic or together? we have some internal models running across both.
[03:18] Maya: main things are prompt format and safety layers. anthropic is more instruction-friendly in some cases - we recommend a brief eval pass to ensure outputs are aligned; redwood has built-in evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. also together's API semantics for chat may differ; again mapping sheet lists those differences.
[03:40] Samir: security and compliance - SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs. we have to pass security review.
[03:47] Maya: redwood is SOC 2 Type II, supports SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations for private deployments. audit logs are available via the console and can be shipped to your SIEM. for dedicated you can have customer-managed keys in the KMS/HSM. i'll attach the security pack (redwood-security.pdf) to the follow-up.
[04:07] Lena: nice. any data residency options? we host in EU and NA primarily.
[04:12] Ravi: yes you can pin region. private deployments also possible if you need on-prem.
[04:18] Oliver: costs - curious about unit economics vs openai. any rough delta?
[04:23] Maya: depends on model and quantization. typical migration to optimized open models on redwood can reduce per-token costs by 40-60% versus the managed openai-type price points for similar throughput; again depends on model and sequence lengths. our optimize product recommends batching and quantization settings for best cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:47] [05:00] Ravi: demo time - i'll run a quick API demo: python snippet to convert an openai chat call to redwood.
[05:05] [05:08] Ravi: show code: old openai: client.chat.completions.create({model: 'gpt-4o', messages: [...]}) -> new redwood: client.chat.generate({model: 'rwd-4o', input: [...]}) - the message format is slightly different (we use 'input' array and 'meta' for conversation state).
[05:28] Samir: will that break our conversation id / session reconciliation? we store message ids and rely on assistant role labeling.
[05:35] Ravi: conversation ids are preserved via 'conversation_id' header - you supply it, redwood returns the same and we also provide 'turn_id' per response. should be straightforward.
[05:47] Lena: are there rate limits or quotas we should expect?
[05:51] Maya: hosted accounts get quota and rate limits per plan; dedicated gets reserved capacity with predictable throughput. we can propose a committed throughput number for your pilot. also we have burst capacity options.
[06:05] Oliver: curious about rolling updates and version pinning - we need stable model versions for audits.
[06:11] Ravi: you can pin model versions and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. the console exposes per-route dashboards and rollout controls.
[06:22] [06:30] Samir: regarding private deployment - if we do a VPC private pilot, what's the onboarding timeline?
[06:36] Maya: for a VPC/private pilot typically 2-4 weeks depending on your infra and whether you want on-prem. dedicated reserved capacity can be faster. for SOC2/enterprise contract there is procurement lead time.
[06:47] Lena: ok, pilot scope suggestion?
[06:50] Maya: propose a 2-week pilot: 100k tokens/day synthetic + your representative prompt set for accuracy and latency benchmarks, one dedicated instance or hosted with reserved burst. we'll run benchmarks, produce a report with p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, and quality regressions.
[07:10] Oliver: sounds good. SLA?
[07:12] Maya: for dedicated we have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has best-effort but with console monitoring. enterprise SLA is part of the contract addendum.
[07:24] Samir: any SDK differences - we use internal wrappers around openai sdk.
[07:29] Ravi: SDKs are similar; we have open-source client libs for node/python/go. the adapters are small. i'll include a compatibility checklist.
[07:40] [07:45] Lena: what about model families - do you have equivalents for openai's ada/curie/davinci etc?
[07:50] Ravi: yes, rwd-embedding-v1 for embeddings, rwd-3b, rwd-7b, rwd-13b, rwd-70b for different tradeoffs. also specialized quantized variants like rwd-3b-q8. the mapping sheet lists recommended replacements per workload.
[08:10] Maya: i want to reiterate the safety net - if you hit quality regressions we have regression alerts and we can rollback to a previous pinned model.
[08:19] Oliver: ok. procurement and legal - we'll need DPA and terms.
[08:24] Maya: yep i'll loop in legal; i'll send DPA and SOC2 report as part of the security pack.
[08:31] Samir: any known gotchas when moving embeddings indices? reindexing time?
[08:36] Ravi: vector dimension and tokenization differences can affect scores; reindexing is recommended. for 10M vectors we can support a staged reindex approach - we'll provide best practices.
[08:49] [09:00] Ravi: quick demo - i'm doing a live call: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RWD_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize feature request."}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.generate - you can see the JSON structure is slightly different but fairly similar.
[09:28] Lena: looks fine. any changes needed for our prompt templating engine?
[09:32] Ravi: templates map to 'system' messages and 'instructions' fields; sometimes token counting differs due to tokenizer edgecases. we included a tokenization comparitor script in the sheet.
[09:45] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
[09:48] Maya: we'll send pricing + pilot proposal (Maya), parity mapping sheet + code examples (Ravi), and security pack including SOC2 and DPA. customer to share prompt set and latency SLOs. schedule benchmark week of 3/30.
[10:05] Oliver: sounds good. any final questions?
[10:09] Lena: none from me. thanks for the thorough mapping.
[10:12] Samir: thanks, look forward to the examples.
[10:16] Maya: great, we'll follow up in email with links: Deck: drive.google.com/example-redwood-migration, Mapping sheet: drive.google.com/example-parity-sheet, Security pack: drive.google.com/example-security.
[10:33] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send the deliverables by EOD Friday. bye.
[10:36] Oliver: bye.

End transcript.
